description: TP tensor_dev_missions.status <-> TensorPhysics research_runtime.TaskStatus mapping (G-A). Rule: every TensorPhysics task status maps to exactly one mission status (to_platform is a function); mission statuses not in the image are platform-only phases owned by the TP approval/lifecycle chain and are listed with a reason. v2 (m4964): added platform_only awaiting_pr_merge — mission_status_vocab v2 / migrations/100_pr_merge_gate introduced the phase on the mission side, and this map file lagged one word behind it; the G-A audit (tools/contracts/vocab_contract_audit.py, item platform_only_consistency) caught the drift. v3 (m5022): added platform_only reopened (mission_status_vocab v3 / migrations/103_mission_reopened) — the post-acceptance governance reopen of SPEC §4.2 has no TensorPhysics TaskStatus image on purpose: it is a governance act on the platform side, not a task phase, and mapping it onto a task state would let a research task be restarted without an acceptance record. New words go into this list, never into a code literal.

mapping.note: backoff between attempts; TP sees running
TP has no cancelled state; m2089 precedent uses stopped

platform_only.reason: acceptance phase owned by TP approval chain
PR open->merge gate owned by TP (migrations/100_pr_merge_gate); no TPh task state maps here
post-acceptance governance reopen (SPEC §4.2, migrations/103_mission_reopened) — independent governance actor + cited acceptance record; deliberately no TPh image

filename_note: Filename keeps the .v1.json suffix on purpose: TensorPhysics pins the copy by filename (it fetches contracts/ from this repo's main). Version field is the semantic source of truth.
